turn_text: Well, John, I want to thank you for having me on today. As you know, I've been working to build the Smithsonian Women's History Museum on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., so we can pay tribute to the women who have contributed so much in our nation's history from Susan B. Anthony who pushed the 90th Amendment to give us the right to vote. to those who helped bring the 19th Amendment, which was, by the way, a Republican Congress that approved it and a majority Republican state that ratified it, to Richard Nixon who signed the Title IX to give women to eliminate discrimination for women and girls in athletics and education programs. And of course, our work to protect women in sports, the first woman to the Supreme Court, Andrew Day O'Connor, all of these individuals, the riveters who worked during World War II, taken on the roles of men in manufacturing to keep our supply chain going. And the black angels from my district in Staten Island, they were nurses who helped find the cure of tuberculosis. This museum, I think, is really an amazing thing. I was very proud this week because President Trump, at his Women's History Month celebration, supported my legislation, supports building the museum on the National Mall. And this is a huge development because this will be part of his legacy and the work that he is doing to support women. As you know, he issued his executive order to protect women in sports. to make sure that men could not compete against girls, because we've seen young women, young girls get hurt, his support for IVF in trying to expand access to it, making our cities and our streets safe. These are all really important issues for women, and I'm really glad that we're going to move forward together with President Trump to find a home on the National Mall, which we already know the land that we want to use, and we've got to transfer that land over so we can get this built.
